description:
The BCH implementation has only fixed-case tests, while its sibling extended-BCH and generic linear-code modules both carry property tests. Add property coverage for the invariants that define correct BCH behaviour.

## Background

The two invariants that matter most are recoverability and syndrome consistency: a codeword corrupted in at most the designed number of positions must decode back to the original message, and a valid codeword must produce a zero syndrome. Fixed cases can pass while the boundary at the correction limit is wrong.

The generator lives in `crates/gf2-coding/src/bch/core.rs`. The existing property-test modules in the same crate establish the shape to follow.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A property-test module in the BCH core covers encode-then-decode round trips with error counts up to the code's designed correction capability, recovering the original message every time.
- [hard] REQ-02: A property test asserts that every valid codeword yields a zero syndrome.
- [hard] REQ-03: Generated cases span more than one BCH parameter set rather than fixing a single code.
- [hard] REQ-04: Cases that exceed the fast tier carry a lowercase `slow:` tagged reason, and the fast tier stays inside its per-test and whole-suite budgets.
- [hard] REQ-05: The new tests fail if the correction limit is reduced, demonstrating that they constrain the boundary rather than only the easy cases.
- [hard] REQ-06: The suite passes, and clippy with warnings denied plus formatting pass.
title: Add property tests for BCH encode and decode invariants
